Subject Further to assistance to the Japanese Gendarmerie.

Made by D.S.I. Pryde Forwarded by C.D.I. Grubb

Sir,
An inquest was held over the body of the deceased, at the Public Mortuary on the morning of 1st. February, 1939 and the following verdict was given.
"Death from natural causes. Body to be removed by deceased friend, Chang Nyoh Yuen.
Procurator: Deng Pai Yue."

With regard to the attached letter signed in the name of "Chang Yen Peng" 80 Chekiang Road. Enquiries show that there is no such house as 80 Chekiang Road neither is there any one named Chang Yen Peng known in that vicinity. The person referred to in the letter as Chen Koo Feng is actually a female named Zung Koo Sze (陳顧氏) who was arrested at 180 Yu Ya Ching Road on 3.1.39 by Crime Branch Headquarters (C.1) at the instigation of the Japanese Gendarmerie. The other person referred to in the letter, namely, Wu Chen, is a doctor at this same address. He has been questioned and denies having any connections whatsoever with mobile units.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
Geo. B. Pryde
D.S.I.

事由：关于协助日本宪兵队之后续事宜。

由副总督察普赖德（Pryde）呈报 经首席侦探督察格鲁布（Grubb）转呈

先生：
1939年2月1日上午，在公立殓房对死者尸体进行了死因研讯，并作出如下裁决：
“死于自然原因。尸体由死者友人张若元（Chang Nyoh Yuen）领回。
检察官：邓柏岳（Deng Pai Yue）。”

关于附信中署名为“张艳鹏（Chang Yen Peng）”、地址为浙江路80号一事。经查，浙江路并无80号门牌，该附近亦无人知晓名为张艳鹏者。信中提及的陈顾凤（Chen Koo Feng）实为一名女性，名为陈顾氏（Zung Koo Sze），于1939年1月3日在亚尔培路180号被总部刑事处（C.1）应日本宪兵队要求逮捕。信中提及的另一人吴辰（Wu Chen）系同一地址的医生。经讯问，他否认与任何流动部队有任何关联。

此致，
敬礼，
乔治·B·普赖德（Geo. B. Pryde）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

REPORT

（印：HEADQUARTERS CRIME BRANCH
File No.
C. I. MISCELLANEOUS FILE
No. Station,
Date January 7, 1939.）

Subject FURTHER TO ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

Made by D.S.I. PRYDE Forwarded by （批：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
D.I. GLOVER.
S. B. D.
Date ）

Sir,

Statements have been taken from the nine persons arrested at the instigation of the Japanese Gendarmerie on the night of 3.1.39 and are attached.

There is nothing in these statements to show that any of these persons have been concerned in any anti-Japanese activities.

The documents seized have been passed to the Special Branch for perusal and report. A superficial perusal of them by the staff of C.I showed that the only document which was in any way suspicious was a copy of the minutes, in book form, of the activities of the " The Nationwide Anti-Japanese Movement" seized at the Pootung Guild.

No members of the Japanese Gendarmerie have visited this office in connection with this case since the last report was forwarded, but D.S.I. Umemoto of the S.P.O. states that they request that these nine persons be handed over to them for investigation.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
（签名：Geo. B. Pryde）
D.S.I.

D. C. (Special Branch).

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of WONG MEI YIEN ( ), 29, M/Unemployed,
native of Wusieh, N.F... taken by me C...S. 172
at Cal on the 5. 1. 39 and interpreted by Yao.

I am now residing in Room 160 Asiatic Lodging House,
Hankow Road. I was brought up in Wusieh (Toong Zah Yuen, Zo
Ko Jico), where I have some 80 mows of land, upon which my aged
mother, wife and children all relied for living.
During March, 1938, after the occupation of Wusieh by
Japanese troops, I was made "head" of that "Hsien"(District)
through the recommendation of Mr.Tsang Chih Lah , in charge of
the 7th. District under the Maintenance Society of Wusieh. The
"Hsien" which I was ruling was infested with bandits. I was
kidnapped from my home at Loh Ko Jico Village at 1 p.m. 12.11.38
by bandits who held me to ransom. As a result of considerable
negotiations with the bandits, I was finally released through
paying a ransom of $2,300.00. It was too dangerous to live in
that "Hsien", and consequently, at the 6.12.38 I and my family
moved to Ngzoh - Aying Fung Village, from there, we boarded
a British s/s "Hen Hsi" and came to Shanghai.
On arrival in Shanghai, I drew $1000 from the Kiangsu
Bank, Kiangse Road, and temporarily put up in Room 160, Asiatic
Hotel, where I am still living. On the 11.12.38, I wrote a
letter to Mr.Tsang Chih Lah (i/c of the 7th.District in Wusieh)
to whom I formally tendered my resignation as head of that "Hsien".
It was my intention to return to my native place as soon as the
war stops. This is the truth.

Signed : WONG MEI YIEN.

以下是黄美燕（ ），29岁，男/无业，吴江籍人士的陈述，由我 C...S. 172 于1939年1月5日在中央捕房录取，由姚某翻译。

我现居住在汉口路亚洲旅馆160室。我在吴江（通泽园，佐科桥）长大，那里我有约80亩土地，我的老母、妻子和孩子都依靠这些土地生活。
1938年3月，日军占领吴江后，经吴江县维持会第七区负责人张芝兰先生推荐，我担任该县“县长”。我所管辖的“县”匪患严重。1938年11月12日下午1点，我被土匪从洛科桥村的家中绑架勒索。经过与土匪的大量谈判，我最终支付赎金2,300.00元获释。在该“县”居住过于危险，因此，1938年12月6日，我和家人搬至ngzoh - 阿英丰村，随后我们登上英国轮船“恒熙”号来到上海。
抵达上海后，我从江西路江苏银行提取了1000元，暂时住在亚洲旅馆160室，至今仍住在此处。1938年12月11日，我致信吴江县第七区负责人张芝兰先生，正式辞去该县“县长”职务。我的打算是战争一结束就返回家乡。以上属实。

签名：黄美燕。

The following is the statement of ZAU Y U K EI ( ), 36, M/shop-propr.
native of Wusieh, taken by me D. S I. Vung Ts Ling,
at C.l on the 5.1.39 and interpreted by YAU

Prior to the outbreak of hostilities, I was proprietor
of the Liang Hsing Lumber Hong at Ting Hong Village, Zoh Ka
Jiao, Wusieh. On 21.11.37, after the occupation of that city
by Japanese Troops, I left for Anhwei, from where I travelled
to Idh Yong. During Feb. 1938, I returned to Wusieh, where I
stayed until 19.6.38, when I boarded Dollar Steam Ship and came
to Shanghai (it was too dangerous to live in my native village
as bandits and kidnappers were in full swing there).
On arrival in Shanghai, I lived in Room 37, Ping Kong
Loding House, Hankow Road for over 20 days. Then I changed into
Room 36 of the same lodging house and lived therein for about
a month. Again I changed into Room 50 and lived for another
month. After that I moved to Room 16S of the Asiatic Lodging
House.
At 1 p.m. 4.1.39, Police raided us and placed my wife
and myself under arrest. I have always been a respectable
business man and I have been in this city for taking refuge.
The proprietors of both Ping Kong and Asiatic Lodging Houses
are my friends. I have never been concerned in any crime.
This is the truth.

Signed : ZAU YAU K EI.

以下是赵玉基（ ），36岁，男/店主，吴江籍人士的陈述，由我副督察长 Vung Ts Ling 于1939年1月5日在中央捕房录取，由 YAU 翻译。

战事爆发前，我是吴江佐家角定洪村良兴木行的店主。1937年11月21日，日军占领该城后，我前往安徽，又从那里前往 Idh Yong。1938年2月，我回到吴江，一直住到1938年6月19日，当时我乘坐美元轮船公司船只来到上海（因为土匪和绑匪在我家乡猖獗，居住过于危险）。
抵达上海后，我在汉口路平康旅馆37室住了20多天。然后我搬到同一旅馆的36室，住了大约一个月。之后我又搬到50室，又住了一个月。此后我搬至亚洲旅馆16S室。
1939年1月4日下午1点，警察突袭了我们，并将我和妻子逮捕。我一直是个正派的商人，来本市是为了避难。平康旅馆和亚洲旅馆的老板都是我的朋友。我从未参与任何犯罪活动。以上属实。

签名：赵玉基。

The following is the statement of ZAU PEU SZ ( )
native of Wusih taken by /s/ C.D.S.I. Vung Ts Ming.
at C.B.H.Q. C.1. on the 5.1.39 translated and interpreted by Hsu

My name is Zau Peu Sz, age 30, native of Wusih, m/female,
and my husband is named Zau Yau Kwei.
In November 1937 our native place Wusih being invaded
by Japanese troops, I evacuated with my husband to Anhwei,
then to Pio-yang where we lived for several months.
In July 1938 we returned to our home in Wusih, where
my husband owns the "Ziang Shing" Timber Company.
As the kidnapping and robbery were prevailing in
the district where I lived with my husband, the latter
then came to Shanghai. Due to my illness I remained in
Wusih until 9.12.38 when, on obtaining a pass, issued by
the Japanese Military Authorities, I took a train to come
to Shanghai. After my arrival at Shanghai I engaged Room
No. 166, Ah Chow Lodging House, Hankow Road.
At about 1 a.m. on 4.1.39 the room occupied by us was
suddenly raided and searched by foreign, Japanese and
Chinese detectives who subsequently brought me and my
husband to C.B.H.Q., S.M.Police, for some unknown reason.
We are all merchants and the above is my true statement.

Signed : - Zau Peu Sz.

我叫赵佩斯，30岁，无锡籍，女，丈夫名叫赵友贵。
1937年11月，我们的家乡无锡被日军入侵，我和丈夫撤离到安徽，然后到萍乡，在那里住了几个月。
1938年7月，我们回到无锡的家中，我丈夫拥有“江兴”木材公司。
由于我和丈夫居住的地区绑架和抢劫盛行，丈夫随后来到上海。我因病留在无锡，直到1938年12月9日，在获得日本军方当局签发的通行证后，我乘火车来到上海。抵达上海后，我租住了汉口路阿周旅馆166号房间。
1939年1月4日凌晨1点左右，我们居住的房间突然遭到外国、日本和中国侦探的突袭和搜查，随后他们以某种不明原因将我和丈夫带到上海公共租界警务处中央捕房总部。我们都是商人，以上是我的真实陈述。

签名：- 赵佩斯。

My name is Zung Koo Tsung, age 47, native of Kashing,

我叫钟古宗，47岁，浙江嘉兴人，女/医生，居住在虞洽卿路180号。

少女时期，我毕业于杭州私立学校。24岁时，我出国前往日本，在东京日本东京医学校学习了4年。随后我回到中国，在奉天辽源医院担任医生一年，并获得了该医院的证书。

My name is Lieu Ts Ming, age 37, native of Kiangyin,,
silk-worn dealer, and residing in Room 31 Zang Tsung Lodging
House, Ching Ho Faung, Chekiang Road.

I was born in Chang Kying Jao, Ho Tang Tsung, Kiangyin
Hsien. I own 7½ mow of land and 3 houses in my native place,
There are 6 members in my family, namely : my mother, wife,
children and myself. I am the only man who supports the
whole family, and I am employed as a manager of the Heng Shing
Silk-worn Hong, Chan, Kying Tsung, Kiangyin.

On 31.12.38 I travelled to Shanghai on board S.S. "Hei-tuh"
and on my arrival at Shanghai I went to engage a room No. 31
in the Zang Tsung Lodging House, Ching Ho Faung, Chekiang Road.

My purpose to come to Shanghai is to check up the business
accounts with my clients in this city. In the noon of 1.1.39
I went to interview Mr. Yu Zia Foo, general manager of the Heng Shing
Silk-worn Hong (Shanghai), No. 57 Tung Chi Li, Sinza Road,
for the purpose of talking over the business accounts with
him. On being requested by me Yu Zia Foo accompanied me and
proceeded to my room in the above said lodging house.
Yu also engages Room 9 in the same lodging house.

Whilst we were reading the accounts books, Woo Chuen
Zuh called on me in the lodging house. (Woo was also arrested)
As Woo Chuen Zuh had no place to live in Shanghai I promised
him to share the room with me without any charge.

I have never held any government positions. I have
been a proper merchant for many years and I have the business
account-books which will testify my statement.

The above is my true statement.
Lieu Ts Ming.

本人名叫刘子明，现年 37 岁，籍贯江阴，绸缎商，现居住于浙江路庆和坊（Ching Ho Faung）藏宗旅馆（Zang Tsung Lodging House）31 号房间。

本人出生于江阴县河塘镇（Ho Tang Tsung）张泾桥（Chang Kying Jao）。本人在原籍拥有土地七亩半及房屋三幢。家中共有六口人，即：母亲、妻子、子女及本人。本人是全家唯一的供养者，受雇于江阴恒盛绸缎行（Heng Shing Silk-worn Hong），担任经理，该行位于江阴陈泾总（Chan, Kying Tsung）。

1938 年 12 月 31 日，本人乘坐“黑土”号轮船（S.S. "Hei-tuh"）前往上海。抵达上海后，本人前往浙江路庆和坊藏宗旅馆租用 31 号房间。

本人来沪的目的是与本市客户核对业务账目。1939 年 1 月 1 日中午，本人前往新闸路同济里 57 号恒盛绸缎行（上海分行）拜访总经理余子甫（Yu Zia Foo）先生，目的是与他商讨业务账目。应本人要求，余子甫陪同本人前往上述旅馆本人的房间。余子甫也在该旅馆租用 9 号房间。

当我们正在查阅账簿时，吴全祖（Woo Chuen Zuh）到旅馆拜访本人。（吴也被逮捕）由于吴全祖在上海没有住处，本人答应让他免费与本人合住该房间。

本人从未担任过任何政府职务。本人多年来一直是一名正当商人，并有业务账簿可以证明本人的陈述。

Formerly I was a rice merchant. I have been running
the Nying Ping Lodging House (located at Poh Koh Village, Kiang-
Ying) for 3 years. During 1938 (March or April), a native
friend, named Yuen Zui Foo and myself put up some capital and
traded in cacoon. The amount which I raised on the first time
was $900, and $300 on the second time. For the 3rd. time, I
put up $500. After the sale of cacoon, I came to Shanghai to-
gether with Yuen per s/s "Kai Tsei" a German liner on 31.12.38.
On 1.1.39 (6 p.m.) I proceeded to see Yuen at his home
situated at 57 Zung Tsi Li, Sinza Road, but he was out. I was
informed by members of his house that he was in Room 9, Zang
Tsung Iding House, Tsing Ju Faung, Canton Road. At once, I went
to the latter place, where we effected a settlement in our deals.
I was given $30.40 at that time, leaving $300 to be paid to me
later. Prior to our arrival in Shanghai, I had already obtained
a sum of $300 from Yuen. Besides I had also received $10 from
him in the form of my salary. The cacoon business yielded to
me a profit of $120.00.
On the early morning of 2.1.39, Police raided this lodging
house and effected my arrest. Lieu Ts Ming was also arrested
in this hotel.
I have never been involved in any crime. This is the
the truth.

SIGNED : WOO KYUIN ZUH.

Sir,
At 9-30 a.m. on 5th January 1939, D.S. Mitsushima
(S.P.O.), D.S.I. Wong Foh Sung and the undersigned accompanied
members of the Japanese Gendarmerie to the Zung Tsaung (慎昌)
watch shop, 685 Nanking Road to conduct a search for possible
literature etc. relating to the movements of mobile units.
Members of the Gendarmerie stated that one named
Wong Pai Zai (黄丕才) was arrested by the military on the
1-1-39 in Japanese - occupied territory and had in his possess-
ion a letter, addressed to him, from one Zung Tsung Liang
(陳正良) who is chief of the 1st section of the Mobile
Unit on the Chekiang and Kiangsu boundaries, asking him to
try and purchase arms and ammunition and forward them to him
(Zung).
On visiting the watch shop it was learned from the
manager that Wong Pai Zai had been employed by the shop for
over two years but, due to recent unsatisfactory work, had
been dismissed on the 12-12-38 and since which date nothing
had been seen of him.
A search of the shop proved fruitless and no arrests
were made.
